meta.method: Second Paris depth pass concentrating on previously empty or structurally obscured walking categories. Famousness alone was insufficient; every retained row is an atomic, legible objective with a current public-access basis, exact feature or route coordinate, two useful sources, a memorable street-level story and global catalogue review.
meta.quality_policy: all retained rows remain draft_only and require field testing before promotion
meta.category_decision: Covered historic commercial passages justify the new globally reusable arcades category. Intact fitted facades for vanished trades justify historicshopfronts and remain distinct from painted ghost signs. Living religious buildings use synagogue or monastery; the quay book trade uses market.

included.s: Two pork butchers opened this black-and-white marble shortcut in 1826 and made perspective part of the sales pitch.
included.w: The diagonal marble grid, repeating shopfronts and low glass roof make a short passage look much longer than it is. It is a compact lesson in how Restoration Paris turned walking, display and illusion into one commercial machine.

facts.claim: Véro and Dodat, both pork butchers, opened the gallery in 1826 on a useful route between Les Halles and the Palais-Royal.
Its diagonal black-and-white floor and repeated fronts deliberately amplify the apparent depth of the passage.
